claims.claim: The game requires an additional large download within the application after downloading the initial files through Steam, with in-game downloads proceeding slowly or resetting if closed.

citations.review_text:
Downloaded 70gb on steam then opened the game to find another 35gb download inside the game itself. This caps at 1MB/s download from their servers but even worse is that's about the speed I get anyway so I can't do anything else while this game is downloading because I can not throttle the download like you can with steam. Pretty weird design. Just make the game 100gb on steam. Makes no sense.

EDIT: I closed the game after it downloaded 5gb out of 35gb. When I reopened it the download has reset. Come on devs it's 2026 you can figure it out. The part that concerns me is where did it download to; because now I need to delete the previously downloaded 5gb of data.

Laggy as ♥♥♥♥ to the point that it's borderline unplayable. Also, the game doesn't download all of its files through Steam. I spent most of my playtime downloading another 30 GB for no reason... but hey, at least it's free.

This wasnt for me. I had a number of issues with it and in 1.6 hours of steam playtime I had a total of 30 mins playtime which is alot less than id normally give a game: 
1) game has a very large file size. which normally wouldnt bother me, but when its bigger than some of the biggest games I do have questions on optimisation/bloat. 
2) the game initially downloads 80GB through steam and then a further 20GB through the game itself, which for whatever reason was alot slower. 
3) game ran poorly on PC (for me) for what is originally a mobile game, I was blown away with the stutters. I dont understand why it ran so poorly and with a 3070 Im a bit shocked how low in the settings i had to get to keep it stable. and when it cut to any cutscene it basically reset my work. 
4) Controls were a bit odd. sprint by default on right click is far from the  standard but might be more for reasons i didnt see for combat combos etc. 

I can see it being fun but as mentioned above as well as poor writing, incredibly slow start, and lack of polish for PC I think this game needs more time to be optimised.

citations.review_text: can be laggy but fun

Really fun game with gorgeous visuals, addictive gameplay and a great exploration loop.

The issue? The game is borderline unplayable on AMD systems. There seems to be a horrible optimization issue regarding shader chaching that causes frequent and long-lasting stutters that flare up even more when entering unexplored areas.

I will gladly recommend the game once this is resolved but not a second before, this is unacceptable.
optimization isnt a thing for this game at all. would be neat if it ran at more than 5 frames a minute

I was never interested in this game, and only decided to give it a shot because I loved Cyberpunk Edgerunners and 2077 so much, and the idea of a more hopeful epilogue of Edgerunners was a pretty huge incentive. That being said, I didn't really play much because the game just refused to work well for me.

It was stuttery almost the whole time to the point that it made combat unfun and often I would outrun the dialogue, which would abruptly end at the start of cutscenes. I don't know if it's a hardware issue, but I run a 5070 so I doubt that's it. It could be an internet issue, since my ping would stay between middling and in the red, but none of my other internet-dependent games suffered these issues.

Extrapolating from the little bit I played, I feel like that this is a decent action game where you occasionally have to pay to keep up with the content. Likely there are better action games that don't have the gacha elements. It's got some cool elements, but nothing worth sticking around for (for me, at least) outside of the Cyberpunk crossover and while I was willing to suffer a mediocre game to get to what I really want, I won't suffer one that is barely functioning, especially since it's easy enough to watch the Cyberpunk content on Youtube.

I really was looking forward towards playing Rebecca, though.

I really wanted to play this game because of the Cyberpunk collab as a certified Lucy liker, but the game is truly unplayable even at lowest settings and optimal conditions. It's rare for me to use the phrase "literally unplayable" and mean it, but there is absolutely no reason for such awful optimisation in an economy where good PC builds are a dream long since vanished.

Guess it's for the best.

claims.claim: The game features fast-paced action combat with mechanics centered around dodging and parrying.

citations.review_text: Wuthering Waves is an incredible open-world action RPG with breathtaking visuals and some of the best combat mechanics in the genre! What I really love is the ultra-smooth, fast-paced combat system featuring parries, dodges, and unique character skills that make every fight feel amazing. The exploration is super rewarding with all the movement tools, and the sci-fi fantasy world is gorgeous. Highly recommend it if you enjoy high-action anime games

With all due respect, as a player who has been playing since release, starting on mobile and eventually moving to a high-end laptop who can play max graphic comfortably with no issues. I still have to say that they need to work on optimisation, it's a shame that not all players can experience the game to its fullest.

I downloaded this for the Cyberpunk Edgerunners Collab and I think that it was worth it. They somehow gave a genuinely amazing conclusion to Lucy's story from season 1 and I think it is honestly one of the best stories I have ever played in a gacha game. However, that is where my praise ends. In order to get to the collab I had to play like 8 hours of the most mind numbing story that had legitimately 0 interesting characters. Solo leveling somehow has a more interesting story and that is crazy because that manwha is devoid of any story. Much like solo leveling this game is carried by hype moments and aura but it somehow forgot how to do both. And I could excuse all of this if the gameplay wasn't just mindless button mashing. It is all style and no substance. Also the main story doesn't even let you use the characters that you roll for over half of the time. It forces you into these prebuilt characters for the plot that make the story missions not challenging at all. This game is not worth your time unless you are going into it for a specific collab because the only characters to give a ♥♥♥♥ about are ones from other franchises that you already care about.

TL:DR Despite the Cyberpunk Collab being good the rest of this game is insufferable ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥.

this game has so many unskippable cutscenes and it's literally just all cutscenes after cutscenes.. like what's the point of getting out of a cutscene walking 2 steps then getting into ANOTHER CUTSCENE!! HOW AM I ON CUTSCENES MORE THAN GAMEPLAY

I'm reviewing the game from a new player experience. I know WW is popular, but this is simply an evaluation of my experience trying it for the first time. 

Friends tried to invite me to the game because I love Cyberpunk, but the onboarding for new players to access this is atrocious. I spent my 4.9 hours on rails experiencing a story climax that I had never taken part in (since it was required to quickly unlock the option to obtain Cyberpunk content) talking to characters I didn't know, had no personal investment in, solving a problem that I STILL don't really understand only to NEVER reach the point where they allowed me to access the banner. 

I ran out of steam and it soured my entire experience with it. Every time I thought they were finally removing my leash, they dragged me back into some other problem I had to solve. I sincerely don't understand why the dev team thought that fast-tracking players into that point of the story was smart or necessary to access the popular event. Once I finish the tutorial simply give me access to the store and all the content as normal. 

Why was this onboarding done this way? You lost a potential customer because you prioritized a story and forced a new player to watch a glorified cutscene for five hours. I barely even had to play or even think about anything I learned in the tutorial because my kit was handed to me and mobs were little more than set pieces. 

Keep in mind I SKIPPED all of the cutscenes I could and it STILL took more than five hours (as I didn't even manage to reach the Cyberpunk banner.)

Despite the lack of playtime on Steam, I experienced the game up to 3.5 content.
So, why not recommending after spending an unhealthy amount of time on that game ?

First, the good : the game is looking good (some zones are gorgeous), and the musics are decent. Also, it doesn't have a Paimon, you can play without an annoyance that can't shut up. 

Saddly, that pretty much sums the good parts of the game.
Next, the bad :

- the monetization is bad, like very bad.... there are worst gatchas on the market sure, but it's nothing to take pride on. The game relies heavily on the FOMO with short pull windows, keeps releasing more and more powerful characters making the previous ones quickly irrelevant for the actual content and use multiple currencies per banner with separate pools. Their 50/50 is disgusting, making sure you waste pulls and you get very few currency in game to try your luck on the newest shinies.

- the story is very generic. It does have shining moments (the Black Shores, parts of Lala-Roi) but in general it won't leave a lasting impact. It also suffers from the gatcha trope of imposing the newest character released in the story to boost up sales, character you may or may not see ever again once its banner is finished, in a attempt to make you cough up money because you feel invested for that time window. It also feels strongly "inspired" by another popular gatcha that may start with Gen and ends with Shin.

- the combat sucks. On one hand, the game emphasis evades and parries, making you think it's closer to a Souls with tactical fighting, but on the other you have complete meat-sack ennemies (even trash mobs), timed combats, and most characters use nervous gameplay with long combos you can't interrupt, else you loose a ton a DPS, and flashy effects. And if you want to clear content in the game, you HAVE to be on the offensive non stop.

It's hard to format my thoughts on this game normally, so I'm going to go with a pros and cons list.

Pros:
- Some of the designs are really good.
- I've really enjoyed the story so far. It's not amazingly written or anything, but I've been entertained by it, and the segments don't feel overly long, or monotonous.
- The combat is really, really fun.
- I love a lot of the voice acting. It's so rare for me (as a British person) to hear British accents in dubs. I really enjoy the variety of VAs.

Cons:
- The game runs terribly unless you have a multi-grand computer.
- The game is really buggy, and will often disconnect constantly, making you completely unable to play.
- The loading screens are really, really long, and sometimes it just crashes in the middle of them, which means you have to sit through MORE long loading screens to get back to where you were.
- The exploration sucks. It's just boring. It feels like such a chore, which is a shame for one of my favourite activities in its competitors.
- The leveling system also sucks. I'm usually a fan of the collect a million different resource gacha game leveling systems, but this one is again, just boring.
- Most of the designs are kind of bad, and quite a lot of them are just terrible. It's a shame because I generally love over-the-top gacha game designs, but this game pushes it too far, to the point that it seems less like the characters are wearing clothes, and more like they went to a scrapyard and threw on bits of everything they saw. They aren't cohesive, and not very visually pleasing.

The game feels weirdly unfinished for a live service game. I don't recommend it, honestly, because its competitors in the genre are just much, much better. i'm someone who's been playing genshin impact since 2021, i've only been playing for nearly 7 days now and i can say... i can never go back.
one of the biggest things, is 100% the skip button. i do like lore, but whenever i want to just focus on combat and actually play or even farming, it's such an awesome tool.

After 40 hours, I can safely say Wuthering Waves is the first gacha in years that actually feels like it respects the player's time.

The combat alone clears most games in the genre. Dodges feel responsive, parries are satisfying, and enemies actually fight back instead of standing there waiting to be hit. Every character feels unique mechanically instead of being another variation of the same kit with different animations.

The biggest surprise for me was how much the game improved over time. Kuro actually listens to feedback and consistently makes meaningful changes rather than pretending community concerns don't exist. Every patch feels like the game is moving forward instead of just selling another banner.

Exploration is rewarding, movement is fast, and the world design encourages you to actually play the game instead of opening a guide every 5 minutes. The soundtrack is underrated, the character designs are great, and the optimization has improved massively compared to launch.

The Cyberpunk: Edgerunners collaboration was also a huge W. Never thought I'd see a gacha pull off a collab that actually fits the game's aesthetic instead of feeling like random marketing.

People keep calling WuWa "just another gacha" but after spending time with it, I genuinely don't see how that's true anymore. It has some of the best action combat on the market right now, gacha or not.

At this point I'm not even interested in going back to certain other open-world gachas. Once you get used to having actual combat mechanics, it's hard to enjoy games where enemies exist primarily as decorative scenery.

Easy recommendation.
10/10

Wuthering Waves has quickly become one of my favorite action RPGs and after spending a significant amount of time with it, I can confidently say it's one of the strongest games in the genre right now. The game's biggest strength is undoubtedly its combat system. Every fight feels fast and responsive with satisfying dodge mechanics, parries, character switching, and combo potential that keep battles engaging. Unlike many games where combat can become repetitive, wuthering waves constantly encourages skillful play and mastery of each character's kit.

The open world is equally impressive. Exploration feels natural and rewarding thanks to the game's excellent traversal mechanics. Running, wall-running, grappling, and moving between objectives rarely feels tedious, along side the early access of flight, exploration becomes a breeze. The world itself is beautiful, featuring detailed environments, impressive lighting, and strong environmental design that make exploration genuinely enjoyable. Hidden puzzles, collectibles, and side activities provide plenty of reasons to wander off the main path.

Visually, the game looks fantastic. character designs, environmental detail, lighting, and combat effects all contribute to a world that feels polished and immersive. every region has its own identity and the attention to detail helps make exploration feel worthwhile. character animations are smooth while combat effects strike a good balance between being flashy and remaining readable during intense encounters.

Another area where wuthering waves shines is its character roster. Each character feels distinct, not only visually but mechanically. Building teams and experimenting with different playstyles adds a lot of depth to the gameplay. The echo system also introduces an interesting layer of progression that rewards longterm investment without feeling overly restrictive.

[h1]Not Recommended (From a New or Returning Player Perspective)[/h1]

I want to be clear: I actually love Wuthering Waves and still actively play it.

The game has a lot going for it. The story is cinematic, the characters are likable, combat is fun and engaging, exploration feels great, and the developers consistently add quality-of-life improvements. The weapon banner system is also much more player-friendly than many other gacha games, with guaranteed 5-star weapons and a lower hard pity cap.

[hr][/hr]

[h2]So Why the Negative Review?[/h2]

Character progression.

If you're a current player who stays caught up with every patch, this issue is less noticeable. For new and returning players, however, it's one of the biggest barriers to enjoying the game.

Almost every character released after Version 1.0 requires materials from regions locked behind later story progression. A new player can pull a character they love from the newest banner, only to discover they can't level that character beyond 30 until they reach the story chapter where those materials become available.

[hr][/hr]

[h2]The Three Choices New Players Get[/h2]

[b]Option A:[/b] Find another player willing to help you access the required region.

[b]Option B:[/b] Rush through large portions of the story, potentially spoiling or diminishing the experience.

[b]Option C:[/b] Leave the character unused until you eventually catch up.

None of these are particularly good solutions.

[hr][/hr]

[h2]The Real Problem: Regional Flowers[/h2]

The issue isn't that materials are story-gated. The issue is that character progression is tied to open-world collectibles.

Bosses, weekly challenge materials, Forte materials, and even Echo progression could all be handled through isolated instances without exposing future regions or story content. Kuro already provides temporary access to certain bosses and weekly materials during character banners, proving this approach is possible.…
